a4_lock: The ninth iron goes into the ninth socket, and the socket takes it the way a lock takes its own key, without argument. The door's slow breathing stops in the middle of a count. Eight irons and a ninth, all nine of them warm, the frame taking up the load, and behind it nothing moving at all for the first time in nine hundred years.
a4_break_die: The tally-die is carried back to the cutting-shop and broken across its own anvil in four strokes, and dwarf steel comes apart in a way that dwarf steel is not supposed to come apart. Ilsabet gathers every fragment into a sack afterwards, on her hands and knees, checking the floor twice. She does not trust fragments of anything, and she says so while she is doing it.
a4_take_ring: The ninth hand's ring lies on the desk where Vale left it, warm and exactly sized for whoever picks it up next. The arithmetic beside it is not complicated: nine irons will hold the lid without a keeper right up until something outside decides to test the arrangement. A count kept honestly by somebody who hates the work is the entire difference between the two situations.
a4_ring_on: The ring goes on, and the count arrives at the back of the skull like a schedule of payments read aloud by a patient clerk. It is not a voice and it is not a compulsion of any kind; it is an obligation, and it is quite specific about dates. The captain of the Ninth Sword stands in a dwarf chapel and understands the shape of the rest of a life.
a4_unmake: This is the decision to unmake the Compact, and it deserves saying out loud. Eight irons in eight warm sockets. Nine hundred years of instalments paid by people who were never consulted about any of it. And a company of five standing in front of the only working arrangement anybody has ever managed with the thing on the other side.
a4_one_at_a_time: One iron out, and the door leans a quarter of an inch outward against its frame. Two, and the stone around the sockets begins visibly to sweat. Three, and the door speaks in the paymaster's voice, and asks with genuine courtesy whether the company has come here to settle the account or merely to increase it.
a4_reseat: Three irons go back into three sockets, put there by hands that are not remotely steady, and the door settles with a sound like a held breath being let out slowly. The paymaster's voice thanks the company by name, all five names, and pronounces them correctly, and then stops.
a4_wedge: The ninth iron is driven crosswise through the socket ring rather than into it, dwarf iron biting on dwarf iron until the entire ring is locked into a single piece that no hand can draw and no keeper can ever count. It is crude, and permanent, and in nobody's written orders.
a4_open: A hand's width of the Ninefold Door, held open on the poleaxe haft with Dellach's boot braced hard against the frame. Warm air comes out of the gap in a rhythm that is not wind and never was wind at any point today. There is light on the other side of it, and the light is not lamplight, and it has no obvious source anywhere.
a4_looked: Behind the Ninefold Door is not a beast in a lair but a hall the size of the hill, with something at the far end of it too large to resolve into any shape at all. Standing in rows in front of that, in Warden cloaks and Fenkin leather and dwarf mail, are eleven hundred people, and every one of them is counting.
a4_lamp_through: A lit lamp is set through the gap on the end of a rope and lowered a foot. It burns steadily for four seconds, then goes out from the wick downward, which is not something lamps do. Then it comes back up the rope, relit by nobody at all, and the colour of the flame is better than it was before.
a4_closed_unlooked: The door is eased shut on nothing seen and the haft withdrawn, and the count resumes precisely where it left off, without any comment. Five people stand in a dwarf gallery having decided together not to know something that each of them will privately want to know for the rest of their lives.
a4_carry: The arithmetic works from the other direction too. Eight irons hold the lid for as long as nobody tests it, but the ninth iron is the count itself, and a count that cannot be kept is a debt that cannot be collected. The ninth iron is currently in your pack, wrapped in salt-cloth.
a4_wrap_iron: Salt-cloth, then oilcloth, then the middle of the pack, with Ilsabet's chalk marks laid across the flap in two directions. The hill's entire attention arrives and settles on five people who are now, quite formally, in possession of the ninth hand's instrument and walking out of the door with it.
a4_withdraw: The honest option gets said out loud in front of the Ninefold Door, by Nyre, who has been assembling the argument for two days and delivers it in about four sentences. This arrangement is nine hundred years old. It is a Warden matter and a Ledger crime, and a company of five people with one commission does not get to be the hinge of it.
a4_take_ledger: Back up to the counting room for four pounds of paper that the Marshal will read carefully and the Ledger will want burnt. The lamp above the table is still lit, and behind the table the clerk's alcove is exactly as it was, with the plaster tally running all the way up to the ceiling.
a4_out: Four hundred steps up, and the hill has revised its opinion of the company. The flights are longer than they were on the way down. The stair-shrine's ninth niche is warm again, all nine lamps in the gallery are lit and trimmed, and at the top of everything the great door has closed to within a thumb's width of shut.
a4_force_gate: Five people, a poleaxe haft, a Warden's shield used as a fulcrum, and eleven minutes of the worst work anybody in the company has ever done. The door gives an inch at a time against a pressure that is not weight, and is not wind, and is plainly not interested in being negotiated with.
a4_chute_out: The spoil chute from below is forty feet of loose scree at an angle that was unpleasant on the way down and is considerably worse now that everybody is tired. The sump behind you is filling steadily and audibly. The lamps in the gallery are going out one at a time, from the far end, working methodically toward the foot of the stair.
a4_postern_out: Out by the mason's postern into weather, with the lead seal broken behind you and the corridor beyond lighting itself politely, one niche at a time, all the way back to the stair. It has the manner of a house showing a guest to the door and watching to see that they leave.
a4_file_out: The ninth hour is waited out in the oil store, and then the file forms on the stair below: nine lamps lifted, the count started, everything on schedule. The Ninth Sword walks out of Kar Duhn in the middle of it with the rhythm right and nobody's hands anywhere they can be seen.
a4_moorback: The Barrow Moor at dawn, with the hill behind you and Gallowmere half a day ahead. The company carries whatever it decided to carry. Nyre asks the question that has to be settled before anybody speaks to a Warden, which is not what happened, but what it is that you are going to say happened.
a4_bothy: Two days in a shepherd's bothy with a peat fire and no watch to keep between anybody. Kettle sleeps eleven hours without moving. Dellach's hands come back to him by the second evening. Ilsabet writes the entire account down twice in case one copy burns, and by the third morning the company remembers how to behave like people.
a4_council: The company council convenes on a wet hillside and runs for an hour. Dellach argues for the Marshal and the written record; Nyre for the Ledger hearing and the naming of Halloway; Kettle for the road south and no names at all. Ilsabet argues for whichever choice keeps the fewest copies of the truth in the fewest hands.
a4_boy: There is a promise to be kept, made in a lamp gallery in front of witnesses and written down in Nyre's book, and keeping it means going back up a hillside that the company has just spent everything it had in order to leave. Dellach is already checking the postern route without being asked.
a4_gallowmere: Gallowmere in the rain again, and everybody is waiting. The Warden's tower has a lamp in the window; a Ledger coach with southern horses stands outside the counting house; the Rooks are in the muster yard pretending not to watch the gate. At the road shrine a woman is lighting candles, and her son is under that hill.
a4_mother: The boy's mother is at the road shrine, and she is told the truth in a wet street by a captain who has been rehearsing the words for two days and gets them wrong regardless. It turns out that she already knew, and had known since midsummer, and that she has been lighting her candles in nines the entire time. She thanks you for coming to her first, which is worse than anything else she could have said.
a4_report: Warden-Marshal Ansel Redd reads it twice, all of it, without asking a single question in the meantime. Then he sets the pages down, squares them, and asks the only three questions that matter to him: what is shut, what is loose, and what exactly is in the company's pack.
a4_record: The written report will outlive everybody in the room: dated, signed by five hands, sealed into the Warden archive at Gallowmere. It requires the captain of the Ninth Sword to set down in plain words precisely what was done to the Ninefold Door, by whom, and in what order it was done.
a4_name_halloway: The Ledger hearing convenes in the counting room with three factors down from the south, and Halloway sits at the end of the table taking his own minutes in that engraved hand. Nyre stands up as a sister of the Reckoning to say that the account is not what the account says it is.
a4_causeway: The causeway into Gallowmere, in rain that has not stopped since the company left it. The stockade ahead, the tower lamp burning at an hour that means somebody is waiting up, and a coach with southern horses standing outside the counting house with its curtains drawn and its driver still on the box.
a4_ahead: Kettle is back from the gate inside eleven minutes with a scout's list, delivered flat and in order of importance. The Rooks are in the muster yard doing nothing, badly, in the rain. A Ledger clerk is taking names at the counting house door, and there are eleven Warden cloaks on the gate that do not remotely fit the men currently inside them.
a4_tower: The Warden's anteroom, with wet cloaks steaming on the pegs and the report copied fair in Ilsabet's hand. You read it through once more while a clerk pretends not to watch the pack that has not left the captain's shoulder since the hill, and has not been set down anywhere at all.
e_a4_completion: The ninth iron is kept, wrapped, and entered on the record as company property held in trust, which takes Redd's clerk two attempts to phrase. Redd's own letter goes south to the Deep Road wardens over his seal that evening. For the first time in nine hundred years the Compact's count cannot be kept at Kar Duhn. And Vale's book lies open on the Marshal's table at the page that lists eight more doors, with the nearest of them under the mountains at the far end of the Deep Road, and a date written against it that falls this winter.
e_a4_win_charter: The writ of salvage is upgraded to a Warden charter with a standing commission and a company seal, and the Ninth Sword is entered in the Marshal's book as a name rather than a hire. The first order issued under it reads, in Redd's own hand: hold the hill, and report the hour of every lamp.
e_a4_win_plain: The ledger is delivered, the ninth iron is handed across a Warden's table and locked into a Warden's strongbox, and sixty crowns are paid in full with the hazard added on without any argument at all. There is a door under the Barrow Moor that is shut tonight, and will still be shut in the morning.
e_a4_win_book: Eleven hundred pages of instalments in nine different hands are laid on a Warden-Marshal's desk, which makes them his problem, his career, and no longer the company's business at all. Redd reads the final twenty pages twice over without speaking. He has the slow attention of a man working out that his own predecessor signed one of them.
e_a4_win_testify: Factor Halloway is named to his face in front of three southern factors, and Nyre matches the ninth signature against his own order-book in open hearing. He does not deny it, which surprises nobody in the room except the factors. A Ledger house discovers that its frontier accounts have been settled in people for eleven years by a man who kept genuinely excellent records.
e_a4_wedge_win: A socket ring locked into a single piece by a ninth iron driven crosswise, reported in plain words and copied out twice for the archive. A Warden request goes south the same week for masons and a mining engineer at Warden expense. What the company did cannot be undone by any hand, and cannot be trusted indefinitely by anybody who understands how old metal ages.
e_a4_win_boy: The promise is kept. In by the postern at dusk, the lamp gallery empty and all nine lamps lit, and the boy found asleep in the oil store where he had been hiding for two days on half a loaf. He goes out over Dellach's shoulder into weather that has never felt better to anybody.
e_a4_silent: A short honest report that says the door is shut and stops there, and the fee is paid, and the company is thanked and released. Four people each know that a decision was taken in a dwarf gallery to leave nine hundred years of arithmetic out of a Warden's file, and none of them raises it again.
e_a4_surety: The ninth iron is handed to the Ledger as surety and entered in its register under a number, which makes it the safest place on the frontier and also the one place the Compact has always been able to reach. The company keeps a receipt that will be worth exactly what the paper is worth.
e_a4_keeper_office: It goes into a Warden file in the captain's own hand: the door is shut, all nine irons are seated, and the count is kept by the captain of the Ninth Sword. There will be a visit to Gallowmere every ninth night for the rest of a life that now has a schedule attached to it.
e_a4_open_admitted: The truth is entered in the record to the inch. The tower is emptied within the hour, the evacuation order is posted by noon, and a company that did the honest thing sits in the muster yard watching a frontier town load its carts on account of a hand's width of open door.
e_a4_reseat_end: Three irons drawn and reseated, written down exactly in those words, and a Warden clerk copies it out twice while Redd asks the question nobody in the room is able to answer. Whether a socket that has been emptied once holds the same as a socket that has never been emptied at all.
e_a4_withdrew: The file records that the company reached the Ninefold Door, described it accurately, touched nothing at all, and came back out again. It is the most defensible sentence anywhere in the Warden archive at Gallowmere. It is also the one that the Ninth Sword will be asked about in every taproom on the frontier for the next nine years.
e_a4_fee: Sixty crowns for the ledger, with no questions invited and none asked by anybody in the tower, and the company is out through the gate before dark with the money split five ways. Nobody says anything much on the road south for the first day. There is an understanding between them, never once spoken aloud, that whatever lies under that hill is now somebody else's arithmetic.
e_a4_bought: The maps, the route, the lamp hours and the company's silence are sold to the Rooks for two hundred crowns and a promise. In spring the Rooks go up to Kar Duhn with eleven people, and nobody at all comes back down to complain about the price that was agreed.
e_a4_south: Gallowmere is skirted at a distance and the Ledger road is taken south with the pack still packed. No report, no fee, no charter, and a ninth iron travelling further from its socket every day in the luggage of five people who have agreed, in some detail, never to discuss it.
e_a4_split: An argument on a wet hillside is allowed to run until it stops being an argument and becomes a settlement. Kettle goes south that same afternoon with her share and her own opinion of the captain. Nyre returns to her order, Dellach walks into the tower alone with his version of events, and the Ninth Sword ends not in a vault but in a disagreement about paperwork.
e_a4_mother_stay: An afternoon in a road shrine with a woman lighting candles in nines, which is the right place for a captain to be and entirely the wrong place for this particular captain today. Redd waits until the fourth hour and then writes in his file that the company did not present itself.
e_a4_jam_fail: The ninth iron is hammered in at an angle to jam the socket permanently, and it works. It also cracks the stone collar around the socket, and a ring of nine that has held for nine hundred years discovers, all at once, that it is now a ring of eight and one wound.
e_a4_unmade: Eight irons are pulled in well under a minute, and the company runs for a stair that is four hundred steps long. It is a plan that requires the door to open slowly. The Ninefold Door has been waiting nine hundred years for the opportunity and sees no reason at all to be slow about it.
e_a4_opened: The fourth iron is drawn while the paymaster's voice is still being courteous about the state of the account, and then the fifth is drawn as well. After that no further decisions are required of anybody standing in the gallery. The arrangement the dwarves engineered has concluded, and the accounts are being settled in the order in which they were originally opened.
e_a4_asked: The question is asked through three empty sockets, and it is answered in full, itemised, with dates and running totals. The figure is one that the company is standing inside of. The door explains, without any heat whatsoever, that a debt does not require the consent of the instalment.
e_a4_wedge_fail: A shoulder is put against a wedged door to establish whether the work holds, which it does, entirely, and would have gone on doing. In the same second the thing on the other side puts its own weight against the same door, out of what can only reasonably be described as curiosity.
e_a4_spoke: One sentence is spoken through a hand's width of open Ninefold Door, in common speech, quite politely. The reply does not arrive as sound. It arrives as arithmetic: the company counted, priced, scheduled, and entered against an instalment that is recorded as falling due immediately.
e_a4_in_for_people: The door is pushed wide and five people walk into a hall the size of a hill to bring out eleven hundred who are standing in rows, counting. It is the most defensible decision anybody makes in this entire story. It adds five to the rows, and changes nothing else at all.
e_a4_lamp: An arm goes through the gap to take back a lamp that has been relit by nobody. The lamp is handed over properly, into the hand that reached for it, by something that has been waiting nine hundred years for a transaction it did not itself have to begin.
e_a4_moor: The ninth iron is sunk in eleven feet of black water in the middle of the Barrow Moor, which solves the problem for exactly one winter. Then the frost lifts the peat, and a fen-runner's boy finds a strip of warm metal in a drained pool and sells it in Gallowmere for two coppers.
e_a4_bait: The ninth iron is carried openly across the Barrow Moor as an invitation, on the theory that whatever wants it will have to come out into daylight and negotiate for it. On the second night the company discovers that it does not have to come out at all, and never has.
e_a4_burn_lamps: Nine lamps are smashed and burning in the gate arch as a gesture on the way out, which feels entirely justified at the time. The hill's answer does not arrive that night. It arrives nine nights later, in Gallowmere, in a file that comes up the causeway at the third hour with its own lamps and its own list.
e_a4_sell_knowledge: Everything the company learned under the hill is sold to Vasse Corrow in a wet muster yard for good coin and no receipt of any kind. The commission goes back to the tower unfulfilled, with an excuse that Redd does not believe and cannot disprove. A Rooks banner goes up the causeway a week later with eleven people beneath it who were told the easy version.
e_a4_ledger_lingered: The plaster tally is chiselled off the alcove wall on the grounds that it is evidence, and evidence is what wins arguments with Wardens. The work takes eleven minutes from first stroke to last. That is about eight minutes longer than the clerk's own arrangement allowed for with whatever it is that comes to read his wall on the hour.
e_a4_sat_down: A captain sits down on the two hundredth step because the legs have finished arguing about it. The company will not leave without its captain, which is the entire point of a company. The stair has been getting longer all evening, and it is in no hurry whatsoever.
e_a4_forced_shut: The great door is held on a shield-fulcrum while five names are called through it in order, which is precisely the arrangement that the shield's dead owner scratched a warning about on its inside face. The fifth name is answered from behind the door, in the captain's own voice, with the correct inflection.
e_a4_chute_out_fall: The strongest goes up the chute first to haul the others, which puts one set of hands at the top and four sets of boots on forty feet of scree that has been waiting all day for a reason to move. It moves while the sump behind them is still filling.
e_a4_file_kept: The file is stayed with to the end of the count, because it is only nine, and the rhythm is easy, and the company is very nearly out. The ninth number arrives on the causeway in open air with the moor plainly visible, and the count starts again from one without any gap at all.
e_a4_boy_lost: The great door is taken because it is faster, and because the boy needs an hour of daylight to walk out in. The door is wide enough for one person going quickly, and then it is not wide enough for anybody at all. The company keeps its promise as far as the threshold and no further than that, and Nyre writes down the hour.
e_a4_ambushed: Kettle's report from the causeway proves accurate in every particular, as her reports generally do. The Rooks are in the yard, a Ledger coach stands outside the counting house, and eleven Warden cloaks on the gate do not fit the men wearing them. The company walks into Gallowmere regardless, because there is nowhere else on this frontier left to walk to.
e_a4_left_with_clerk: A fair copy of everything is left on a clerk's desk with the company's five names on it and no witness to the handing over of it. Redd reads it eleven days later, by which time the coach with the southern horses has been back to the counting house twice and left again.
